title: Observe: one unsure moment, and what you actually saw
outcomes: Separates an observation (what you can point to) from a guess (a prediction or judgment)
Knows that some guesses can be tested
Writes down one unsure moment per game

steps.text: **Observe** before you judge. An **observation** is something you can point to on the board or the clock: 'my queen is attacked by a knight', 'I had two minutes left'. A **guess** is a prediction or a judgment: 'I am lost', 'he will win my pawn'. Guesses are fine. Label them, and test the ones that can be tested.

steps.title: Guesses can be tested
steps.prompt: Each note is an observation or a guess. For a guess, predict whether a test will confirm it, then check.

steps.text: **One unsure moment per game.** After each game choose one move where you felt unsure. Write: the move number; what you could see (observations); what you guessed; what would settle it. Do not ask an engine yet. One moment written down beats a long review you never finish. This is a habit to try.

**What the app does for you now, and when it stops.** After each practice game the form below asks for one unsure moment. The plan is to ask only after every third game, then only when you open the form yourself (a first guess, to be changed by what you actually do). Exporting your notes as plain text is planned, so they stay yours.

steps.prompt: Use your last game, or the position from the item you just solved. Pick ONE moment where you were unsure and fill in the four lines. Keep observation and guess apart.
